pages.text: Plants take six nutrients from the soil:$(li)$(thing)Nitrogen (N):$() leaves and protein. Mobile: washes out with drainage, worst in sand.$(li)$(thing)Phosphorus (P):$() roots and seed. Locked up in very acid or very alkaline soil.
$(li)$(thing)Potassium (K):$() water use and quality. Held by clay.

$(li)$(thing)Sulfur, Calcium, Magnesium:$() needed in smaller amounts; calcium matters for peanuts and tomatoes.$(br2)Growth is limited by whichever nutrient is shortest (Liebig's law of the minimum). Adding more of the others does nothing.

Each crop needs a different amount: maize and cabbage are heavy feeders, while legumes make most of their own nitrogen. Micronutrients (iron, zinc, manganese) become scarce above pH 7.5, and sensitive crops then yellow.
